title: Higher Resolution Sprite s and Tilesets

posts.author: Burrito8
posts.body:
Hi everyone! I'm new to this forum and have a question about image sizes/resolution when it comes to sprite character sheets and tilesets on RMMV:
I have the default tile size set to 48 x 48 and have been using Photoshop to modify existing character sheets with some custom characters. The problem is, when I reduce these images to fit the tiles, the images are pretty blurry and pixelated. I also saw a post who said their character sheet was something like 5184x3456.
I can make my character sheets this size too, but then the characters look like giants (like, only their feet are visible onscreen). Is there a plug-in or code I can use to have higher resolution images that scale down and still fit within RPG Maker's tiles?
Thanks a bunch!

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
In 2D, the pixel is the absolute unit. reducing pixel numbers always means a loss of information and thereby a loss of quality.
the physical resolution is measured in pixel per distance - by default 48 pixel per tile.
So increasing the resolution means increasing the pixel per tile.
so if that is what you want you can look for a change tilesize plugin.
However, because nothing can change the editor, you'll have to use some additional worki to use larger tilesizes.

You've already been given an answer to this. A pixel is a pixel.
If you want to have images that are "high resolution," that's by definition over a certain number of pixels in dimensions. If you scale them down in an image editor, they're taking up fewer pixels - there's literally nothing on your monitor to continue displaying the same details.
That's like saying "I want this wall of my house to only be six inches long, but I still want a window there" - there physically isn't the space to put it.
I'm not sure what you'd want the plugin to do for you.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Burrito8 said:
Does anyone know if manually increasing the screen width and height is the best way to get higher resolution characters, or is there a plug-in that could do this?
Click to expand...
A higher resolution is more pixels per tile - and since the pixels are fixed, that means less tiles in the same area.
increasing the screen size is NOT the same as making a higher resolution, despite the screen size being falsely called a resolutionby Windows settings. That is why I specified "physical" resolution in my answer above.
Increasing the screen size will only increase the number of tiles that fit into your monitor area.
The effect you probably want would need both at the same time - for example doubling the pixel per tile AND doubling the screen size would result in the same number of tiles on the screen, but those tiles having double the pixels per dimention on display.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
You still don't seem to understand the terminology you're using.
Something that's "high resolution" still uses the same pixels on your monitor.
The vast majority of people have a 1920x1080 display, so you can only use a sprite that's 1080 pixels tall and have it all be visible (and that one sprite will take up the entire height of the monitor). It makes
no difference
what game engine you use.
You can only use larger images than that if you're making your game exclusively for people who have 4k monitors or whatever. Or if you're using a 3D engine so that the entire image
doesn't
fit on the screen at one time and you're looking up and down to see the entire thing.
I have no idea where you got that 5184x3456 number from, but if that's a single-actor character sheet, it means each cel is 864 pixels tall and 1,728 pixels wide - that's almost the entire screen for a 1080p,
high def
resolution.
If there's something you don't understand, please ask for clarification - but it seems like you keep asking the same question with the same words to different people, hoping to get a different answer.
